open_questions: The Iowa-era kit: Equipboard's community notes have an Orange County Drum & Percussion kit (and a 13x7 maple snare) on the Iowa tour and Pearl Masters MMX from the Subliminal Verses tour; Songsterr tabbers label tracks both ways. Confirm from a dated interview or photograph.

Find the Drum! magazine interview Drumeo quotes ('Double bass needs to be used as a dynamic, not for flash') and the Modern Drummer covers (2002, 2004) for his own words of the Slipknot years; the interviews read here are from 2016 and 2017.
Name the R&B and jazz teacher Wikipedia mentions, and the school drum corps he told Bonedo about.
Songsterr's tempos run high (People = Shit's blast at 216, The Heretic Anthem at 199): beat-track the records before trusting them.
Whether the Iowa blasts are on one kick or two, and whether he played heel-up: no source read says.
No drummer was found naming him as an influence in their own words beyond Jay Weinberg's regard; the Rhythm and Loudwire polls are readers' votes.

identity.name: Joey Jordison
identity.summary: Slipknot's drummer, #1, from its first shows in 1995 until his dismissal in 2013, and the one who named the band; with Paul Gray he wrote most of Iowa. He brought thrash and death metal's double bass and blast beats into a band that sold millions: traditional and 'hammer' blasts on People = Shit, continuous sixteenths on two kicks, chinas on the beat, half-time choruses with the kick pushing the bar line, and fills dropped where nobody expected them. Masked, in the band's jumpsuit, on a riser that lifted and tipped the kit over the crowd. Also Murderdolls (on guitar), Scar the Martyr, Vimic and Sinsaenum; filled in for Lars Ulrich at Download 2004. Transverse myelitis took the use of his left leg near the end of his Slipknot years; he recovered and played again. He died in 2021, aged 46.

persona.description: Slipknot's members were numbered 0 to 8, each in a mask of their own and the band's matching jumpsuit; Jordison was #1. The masks were remade for each album to show each member's growth.
persona.costume: A white, expressionless kabuki-style face mask he painted himself: black round the eyes, black lips, and black and dark red streaks running up the brow and down the cheeks from the eyes (Iowa era, Disasterpieces 2002); long black hair worn over and round it. The band's jumpsuit with his #1. For All Hope Is Gone (2008) a crown of thorns and warped stitches were added to the mask.

evidence.note: The mask is described from the 2002 footage; its make (a Cesar kabuki mask) is from Equipboard, community-sourced.

institutions.name: High school drum corps
institutions.outcome: 'I learned a lot about stick control there, and benefited from it later.'

traditions.tradition: His parents' and uncle's rock records
traditions.impact: Tattoo You at five, Quadrophenia, Led Zeppelin I to IV and In Through the Out Door; his uncle played him Bonham's solos and Rush's 2112.
Reign in Blood in his Easter basket in 1986; trying to keep up with Benante's double bass on Anthrax's A Skeleton in the Closet; his first serious band, Modifidious, played speed and thrash metal.
Self-taught at first, then a teacher of R&B and jazz technique although he wanted to play metal.
He learned by taking his favourite records and the drummers he admired and playing along.

formative_events.event: His parents gave him a first kit; he had played guitar before it.
Paul Gray invited him to a rehearsal of the band that became Slipknot; he joined on drums, moving Shawn Crahan to percussion, and later suggested the name.
Played eight of Metallica's thirteen songs at Download when Lars Ulrich could not: "one of the biggest fucking dreams come true".
Slipknot announced on 12 December that he had left; he said he had been fired. In 2016 he revealed transverse myelitis, which had cost him the use of his left leg.

eras.label: Debut
eras.context: Meld, Mate. Feed. Kill. Repeat. (1996) and the first album with Ross Robinson; co-mixed by Jordison.

eras.label: Iowa
eras.context: Written mostly with Paul Gray; the fastest record and its tour, filmed for Disasterpieces in London, February 2002. Murderdolls on guitar from 2002.

eras.label: Vol. 3 and All Hope Is Gone
eras.context: Rick Rubin, then Dave Fortman; Download 2004 for Metallica, Korn in 2007; the riser that turned him upside down on the All Hope Is Gone tour.

eras.label: After Slipknot
eras.context: Scar the Martyr, Vimic and Sinsaenum, after recovering from transverse myelitis.

evidence.note: No measurement found.

swing.notes: Straight throughout; no shuffled part found in the tabs read.

dynamics.balance: Loud and even: rimshot backbeats, triggered kicks, chinas and open hats; a ghost note now and then (Duality).

feel_profile.interaction: With the riff: the kick doubles the guitars, the choruses drop to half time, and two percussionists (Crahan and Fehn) play over him; 'Songs are not drum solos.'

hand_techniques.name: Traditional blast
hand_techniques.description: Kick and snare alternating with the china on the kick (People = Shit, Disasterpiece).

hand_techniques.name: Hammer blast
hand_techniques.description: Kick, snare and china in unison on every note.

hand_techniques.name: Sextuplet and 32nd fills round the kit
hand_techniques.description: A one-bar 32nd fill across the kit (People = Shit); a sextuplet 'four hands, two feet' fill (Psychosocial); a sextuplet snare roll with china accents.

hand_techniques.name: Stick control
hand_techniques.description: From years in a school drum corps.

foot_techniques.name: Continuous double bass
foot_techniques.description: Sixteenths on two feet under open hats or a china (The Heretic Anthem; Disasterpiece at 210); used as a dynamic, not for flash.

foot_techniques.name: A double pedal on one bass drum, two bass drums on the riser
foot_techniques.description: Two 22x18 bass drums in his kits, but in 2017 the Demon Drive double pedal played only the right one.

devices_search.note: None found. Every tab read is in 4/4 (a single 2/4 bar in three of them). The groupings of three in Before I Forget's mosh part (Bonedo) and the 3+3+2 kicks of Duality and Wait and Bleed follow the riff inside the bar: no cross pulse and no cycle across the bar line. His sextuplet and 32nd fills are subdivision and speed, not a device.

voice_language.hihat: Open eighths in the verses (Duality, Psychosocial, Wait and Bleed, The Heretic Anthem).
voice_language.snare: Rimshot backbeats on 2 and 4, or on 3 in the half-time sections; alternating with the kick in blasts.
voice_language.kick: With the riff in the grooves; continuous sixteenths on two feet; the last sixteenth of a half-time bar.
voice_language.toms: Fills round the kit in 32nds and sextuplets; tom figures over kick eighths (Psychosocial).
voice_language.cymbals: Chinas on the beat in choruses and blasts; two crashes by turns (Disasterpiece); Paiste RUDE and 2002.

implements.notes: Ahead JJ1 sticks early, Promark (his TX515W) from 2005, wrapped in grip tape.

aesthetic: dense band mix with two percussionists
sound_profile.cymbal_character: Paiste from May 2001: RUDE and 2002 chinas (15 to 21 inch), RUDE crash/rides, 2002 Wild hats, Signature splashes.

by_era.description: Ross Robinson and Andy Wallace: dense, abrasive, the kick triggered and fast enough to read under the guitars.
Rick Rubin and Greg Fidelman (Vol. 3), more room; Fortman and Colin Richardson (All Hope Is Gone).

sample_hints.iowa: Tight metal kit: punchy, clicky kicks, a high cracking snare, big chinas.

signature_traits.label: Blast beats in the charts
signature_traits.description: Traditional and hammer blasts on an album that went to the top of the charts: Iowa is 'one of the few mainstream albums' with blast beat percussion.

signature_traits.label: Double bass as a dynamic
signature_traits.description: Death-metal double bass brought into the mainstream after Metallica and Slayer, and placed where it lifts a section: 'Double bass needs to be used as a dynamic, not for flash.'

signature_traits.label: Half-time with a push
signature_traits.description: Choruses dropped to half time, china on the beats, the kick on the last sixteenth pushing into the next bar.

signature_traits.label: Fills where you do not expect them
signature_traits.description: Snare hits and fills in unexpected spots while keeping the song's part: 32nds round the kit, sextuplet rolls with china accents.

signature_traits.label: The riser
signature_traits.description: The kit on a hydraulic riser that lifts and tips it toward the crowd (Iowa tour, 2002), later turning him upside down in a harness.

signature_traits.label: #1, masked
signature_traits.description: A white kabuki-style mask he painted himself, under long black hair, in the band's jumpsuit with his number.

patterns.name: People = Shit: the 'hammer blast'
patterns.function: The end of the intro: kick, snare and china struck together on every eighth

patterns.name: People = Shit: the half-time chorus

philosophy.idea: Double bass is a dynamic, not flash.
Songs are not drum solos: get your chops right first, or the song will never be right.
Speed comes with persistence: don't be discouraged when it doesn't work at once; there is a threshold.

innovations: Blast beats and death-metal double bass on million-selling records
The nu metal drummer as a technical player
The tilting and rotating drum riser as part of the show

accolades.award: Rhythm readers' poll: best drummer of the previous 25 years
Loudwire readers: the world's greatest metal drummer

cultural_references.description: Filled in for Lars Ulrich with Metallica at Download 2004.

common_misconceptions: That he left Slipknot: he said he was fired, and only later revealed the transverse myelitis that had taken his left leg.
That Slipknot's drumming is all one man: two percussionists, Crahan and Fehn, play over him.

beatbreaker.default_kit_sound: Tight metal kit: punchy, clicky double kicks, a high cracking rimshot snare, chinas
generation_rules: Straight sixteenths; no swing, few ghost notes.
Blasts at 200 to 220: kick and snare alternating with the china on the kick, or kick, snare and china together.
Continuous sixteenths on two kicks under open-hat eighths or a china for the heavy sections.
Choruses in half time: china on the beats, snare on 3 (or 2 and 4 at the slower tempo), the kick on the last sixteenth.
Kick with the riff in threes inside the bar; open hats on the eighths in verses.
Fills in 32nds and sextuplets round the kit, sometimes where the phrase does not ask for one.

lineage_display.lineage_blurb: Reign in Blood in an Easter basket, Benante's double bass, Bonham and Peart from an uncle's records; then eighteen years as Slipknot's #1.
